kivi_style_kv_quant.scheme: asymmetric min-max grouped quantization; keys per-channel (grouped along tokens), values per-token (grouped along head_dim)
kivi_style_kv_quant.applied_to: stored KV cache (streaming, after each prefill chunk and each decoded token)
kivi_style_kv_quant.note: Tensors are round-tripped through the target bit-width and kept in bf16, so quality is exact for the scheme while the memory figure is analytical. Tokens that do not fill a per-channel key group stay in full precision and are charged at 16 bits.

snapkv.adaptation: Upstream's monkeypatch targets transformers==4.37 and Llama/Mistral/Mixtral; this runs transformers 5.x on Qwen2, so SnapKVCluster is driven directly. Attention scores are pooled across each GQA group's query heads so selection is per KV head; upstream instead stores KV repeated to the query-head count.

streaming_llm.adaptation: Applied to the resident prompt cache; policy is upstream's, unmodified.

kv_merging.scheme: temporal mean-pooling of consecutive KV states, sinks and recent window preserved
kv_merging.applied_to: resident prompt cache, one-shot after prefill

low_rank_kv.scheme: per-head mean-centred truncated SVD (randomized, niter=2) of the prompt K and V
low_rank_kv.applied_to: resident prompt cache, one-shot after prefill
low_rank_kv.note: Reconstruction is written back in bf16; the memory figure is the U/S/V factor size.

dkv_mid.adaptation: The repository's serving runtime owns its own paged block pool and a Triton decode kernel that is unavailable on Windows. The block compressor is therefore driven directly over the resident prompt cache and its output reconstructed in place, which measures the representation's fidelity and size but not the runtime's sparse-decode speedup.
dkv_mid.entry_point_limitation: Upstream has two public block-compression entry points and they do not share a residual selector. CRBench calls compress_lowrank, whose residual selection is the token_norms path. The run-atomic and query-scoped work added in ef750011 lives in _compress_layer_blocks_gpu_inner, reached only through compress_layer_blocks_gpu(blocks_list, manager=...), which needs the paged block-pool objects the serving runtime builds. Refreshing the vendored repository from ad4d6708 to ef750011 therefore left every number here unchanged, which was verified rather than assumed: b_eff and quality matched at all five context lengths on Qwen2.5-7B. These results characterise DKV's standalone block compressor, not its full runtime.
dkv_mid.query_pinning_note: Upstream's residual reservation defaults to DKV_RESIDUAL_RUN_RESERVE='query_first', which scopes exact residuals to a question pinned by the serving layer through KVRuntimeManager._pending_query. CRBench does not supply it, so DKV runs its no-query fallback and reserves residuals by reconstruction error; run-atomic selection still applies. This is a fairness decision, not an oversight: every method here sees the same prompt and nothing else. Handing one method a separate, structured 'here is the question' signal that the others never receive would measure how well the harness was tuned for it rather than how the representation performs. SnapKV's observation window is not an exception -- it reads the last tokens of the prompt the model was already given, which is the method's own mechanism operating on ordinary input.
